passages.scripture: Once again Jesus entered the synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.

lines.text: Jesus went into the synagogue again.
Something withered has dried up and shriveled, like a plant that dries up.
A man whose hand was withered was in the synagogue.

passages.scripture: In order to accuse Jesus, they were watching to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.

lines.text: Some people in the synagogue watched Jesus closely to see if He would heal the man with the withered hand on the Sabbath.
Those people considered healing to be work, and God’s law said no one should work on the Sabbath.
If Jesus healed on the Sabbath, those people wanted to accuse Jesus of breaking God’s law.

passages.scripture: Then Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Stand up among us.”

lines.text: Jesus said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand in the middle.”
So the man would stand in the middle of the synagogue, where everyone could see him.

passages.scripture: And He asked them, “Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?” But they were silent.

lines.text: Jesus asked the people watching Him a question.
Jesus said, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good, or to do evil?”
Jesus said, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath to save a life, or to destroy a life?”
If doing good is lawful on the Sabbath, then healing the man is lawful on the Sabbath.
But the people watching Jesus kept silent — the people watching Jesus would not answer what Jesus asked.

passages.scripture: Jesus looked around at them with anger and sorrow at their hardness of heart. Then He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” So he stretched it out, and it was restored.

lines.text: Jesus looked around at the people watching Him.
Hardness of heart is a stubborn refusal to accept the truth — even after seeing it.
Jesus felt anger and sorrow at the hardness of heart of the people watching Him.
Then Jesus said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.”
So the man stretched out his hand.
To be restored is to be made healthy again, as it was before.
The hand of the man was restored.
So Jesus healed the man on the Sabbath, in front of the people watching Him.
